title: Choose Shortn's visual world
question: The roll picked Registered Post. Keep it, choose an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Registered Post
options.lineage: CTT registered-mail labels, airmail envelopes, postmarks, franking meters, sorting-office dispatch ledgers
options.thesis: Each link is an addressed label: a key, a destination, and a trail of postmarks as people pass through it.
options.viewport: The Links ledger: an addressing bar sits on top; below it every link is a label row with a heavy-grotesque key, a routed destination, and wavy postmark cancellation lines that show the last 7 days of clicks.
options.risk: Becomes a costume if the postal motifs show up as ornament instead of carrying state (routing, cancellation, franking).

raised.raise: The QR library is a perforated stamp sheet packed edge to edge in whole cells, with a code under each stamp.
QR modules and the S mark only ever render at whole-pixel multiples, so previews are print-honest.
State changes stamp in as a 90ms two-frame thunk. Nothing fades or floats.
Plan usage is a franking meter that always shows exactly how much capacity is left. Limits are never hidden.
Postal red is reserved for one role only: the live route and the primary action.

options.label: Prepress Proof
options.lineage: print-shop proof sheets, crop and registration marks, colour bars, imposition sheets
options.thesis: Every link is a proof on press, checked digitally and in print, signed off and run.
options.viewport: Links laid out as an imposition sheet. Crop marks frame each row, a CMYK control strip doubles as the usage meter, and the QR preview sits at true print size.
options.risk: The most familiar route for a print + digital product, and the one most runs here would land on.

options.label: Emission-Line Rail
options.thesis: Click history drawn as hairline emission lines along one calibrated time rail.
options.viewport: Analytics as a single rail: every click is a line, and state is shown by line height and dash pattern.
options.case: Strong analytics clarity because state is carried by line form, not hue. Marketers don't recognise themselves in it.
options.risk: Cold and lab-like for a marketing team, and it fights the navy brand.

options.label: Convention Catalog
options.thesis: Thousands of stamp-size cells packed into a numbered hall grid.
options.viewport: A dense numbered grid of thumbnails.
options.risk: Pop-culture world foreign to newsroom marketers.
options.kept: Edge-to-edge whole-cell grid → QR stamp sheet.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.risk: Retro novelty; poor fit for long working sessions.
options.kept: Integer-honest rendering → crisp QR and mark.

options.label: Acetate Tab Manual
options.thesis: Sections as hued divider boards under acetate leaves.
options.viewport: Stepped tab rail down the fore edge.
options.risk: Rainbow section hues overrule the navy brand.

options.label: Mixtape J-Card
options.kept: Capacity always visible → honest franking meter.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: A purple course riding over fixed terrain.
options.risk: Niche sport; marketers won't read it.
options.kept: One reserved colour only for the active leg.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A Dub/Linear-style SaaS dashboard at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, a filter bar, and a dense links table with sparkline columns.
canonCard.risk: Looks like the competition by design.
